summary: A specialist in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Robert DeCaroli earned his MA and PhD at UCLA under Robert L. Brown and Katherine Anne Harper. He lectured at UCLA and Loyola Marymount before joining George Mason University around 2004.

Working in Indology and religious studies, Robert Deliège studied at the University of Oxford from around 1981 to 1986. He held posts at the University of Kerala and became a professor at the Université catholique de Louvain around 1989.

Robert Duquenne was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He held a post as a specialist in Tantric Buddhism at Hōbōgirin (attested 1981) and was later affiliated with the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2009).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Robert E. Buswell Jr. studied under Kusan Sunim, Lewis Lancaster, and others, earning his AB, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley. He served as Professor and Distinguished Professor Emeritus at UCLA from around 1986 to 2022.

Robert E. Harrist, Jr. works in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Columbia University, attested in 2009 and later attested in 2026 as Jane and Leopold Swergold Professor Emeritus of Chinese Art History.

A scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, Robert E. Morrell studied under doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis, attested in 1985 and 2006.

Working in Indology, Robert E. Svoboda studied at the University of Oklahoma and mentored under Aghori Vimalananda (~1975–1983). As of 2008, he held adjunct posts at The Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.
Robert F. Rhodes works in Buddhist studies and Japanology and was a PhD candidate at Harvard University. He served as a professor at Otani University, attested during 1993–2000 and 2012–2014.

Robert Florida works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University and later as an Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria (attested 2000–2005).

A scholar of Sinology and religious studies, Robert Ford Campany was a professor at Indiana University Bloomington (~1989–2006). He later held posts at the University of Southern California (~2006–2010) and Vanderbilt University in 2010.

Robert Gardner studied at Harvard University (BA ~1943–1947), founded it in 1957, and served there as a professor from 1956 to 1997. He also worked at the Harvard Art Museums and taught medieval art and history at the University of Puget Sound.

Robert Gauthiot worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1898–1904) and became a member of the Société Asiatique in 1909.
Robert Göbl was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna from 1947 to 1950 and held a post there from around 1955 to 1989.

A Japanologist, Robert H. Brower studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan. He taught at Minnesota and Stanford, directed the Inter-University Center for Japanese Language Studies (1963–1964), and chaired Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan (1966–1988).

Robert H. Sharf works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned degrees from the University of Toronto and the University of Michigan, later holding faculty posts at McMaster, Michigan, and UC Berkeley, where he was appointed Distinguished Professor around 2004.
Robert Hinde studied at St John's College (~1942–1948) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1948–1950). He subsequently held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from around 1950 to 1994.

Robert J. Miller was a scholar in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1955–1989) and also held a professorship at the American Institute of Indian Studies.
Robert J. Topmiller specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Kentucky under the supervision of George C. Herring.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Robert Kritzer earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held posts at UC Berkeley and served as Associate Professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).
Robert Kyd studied at the University of Edinburgh. In 1787, he founded the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden.
